Content:
There is a linear correlation between two sets of paired observations if the data points on the corresponding scatter plot are located along a straight line.

Content:
We say that the correlation is positive if the corresponding trend line has a positive slope. Similarly, we say that the correlation is negative if the corresponding trend line has a negative slope.

Content:
We have a strong correlation if the data points lie close to the corresponding trend line. Similarly, we have a weak correlation if the data points are scattered far from the corresponding trend line.

The linear correlation coefficient [MATH: \rho] (the Greek letter rho, pronounced "row") is a real number between [MATH: -1] and [MATH: 1] that shows the strength of a linear correlation. It has the following properties:

Content:
- [MATH: \rho = 1] indicates a perfect positive correlation
- [MATH: \rho = -1] indicates a perfect negative correlation
- [MATH: \rho = 0] indicates no (linear) correlation

sections.normalized_html:
Recall that the linear correlation coefficient [MATH: \rho] satisfies the inequality [MATH: -1 \leq \rho \leq 1,] where [MATH: \rho = 1] indicates a perfect positive correlation, and [MATH: \rho = -1] indicates a perfect negative correlation.

With that in mind, let's examine our scatter plot.

We note the following:

  • The points in the scatter plot seem to follow a straight line with a positive slope. So, the correlation coefficient must be positive. Thus, we disregard the following value: [MATH: \rho = -0.8]

  • The points lie pretty close to the corresponding trend line. So, the correlation coefficient must be closer to [MATH: 1.] Thus, we disregard the following value: [MATH: \rho = 0.3]

Therefore, the best approximation of the correlation coefficient from the given options is [MATH: \rho= 0.9.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

There is a linear correlation between two sets of paired observations if the data points on the corresponding scatter plot are located along a straight line.

We say that the correlation is positive if the corresponding trend line has a positive slope. Similarly, we say that the correlation is negative if the corresponding trend line has a negative slope.

Content:
We have a strong correlation if the data points lie close to the corresponding trend line. Similarly, we have a weak correlation if the data points are scattered far from the corresponding trend line.

[MATH: -1 \leq \rho \leq 1,]
where [MATH: \rho = 1] indicates a perfect positive correlation, and [MATH: \rho = -1] indicates a perfect negative correlation.

Therefore, since [MATH: \rho \approx -0.85,] there is a strong negative linear correlation in the data.

- The negative linear correlation means that the data points should be scattered along a line with a negative slope.
